values.binary_distribution_rule: Yes equals the reported percentage; No equals 100 minus that percentage.

analysis_claims.universe: Endpoint-specific valid baseline/follow-up pairs among returned households, preserving original assignment and observed noncompliers. Eligible bases are all enrolled households within arm. Baseline missing counts cover all enrolled; post numeric missing counts cover returners.
analysis_claims.weighting: Supplied fixed weight_base. Both wave levels and mean respondent-level change use the same pairs within each endpoint and arm. No attrition correction.

analysis_claims.universe: Independent valid-case distributions at baseline and follow-up, respectively; distinct from endpoint-specific paired assignment estimates.
analysis_claims.weighting: Fixed weight_base on each exact valid-case set. Different denominators must not be combined into a conversion funnel or interpreted as incremental campaign change.

values.arm_balance_numeric_missing_rule: Eligible N minus valid N within each stated universe. Restricting to returners separately excludes 330 control and 381 assigned households.

analysis_claims.universe: Return rates use all enrolled households. Baseline profiles use valid answers within return-status or assignment groups; arm balance among returners is examined separately.
analysis_claims.weighting: Fixed weight_base. Profile differences are descriptive; weighting does not recover missing follow-up outcomes.

analysis_claims.universe: Receipt uses all enrolled households. Recall uses valid recall among returners. Concordance uses returned valid-recall respondents. Observational consideration uses the same consideration pairs at both waves, additionally restricted to valid recall for recall grouping.
analysis_claims.weighting: Fixed weight_base within each stated universe. Receipt and recall group differences are descriptive associations, not assignment effects.

analysis_claims.universe: Stress uses valid baseline responses by children under 18. Heterogeneity uses endpoint-specific observed pairs in four disjoint assignment-by-children cells. Interaction is the children minus no-children assignment contrast.
analysis_claims.weighting: Fixed weight_base. Stress is descriptive. Interaction variances sum the four independent cell mean-change variances; Holm adjustment applies to the three interactions.

analysis_claims.universe: Returned respondents with recorded recall=Yes. Each item uses valid 1–5 scores; each correlation uses pairwise-complete scores.
analysis_claims.weighting: Fixed weight_base. Descriptive distributions and coded-score Pearson correlations only; no significance search or causal driver model.

analysis_claims.universe: Returned respondents recording usage_post=Yes; valid item responses within this selected four-week-user route. Usage days concern the previous seven days, for which zero is valid.
analysis_claims.weighting: Fixed weight_base. Descriptive user experience only; neither an assignment effect nor evidence about nonusers.

findings.proposition: Assignment supports an awareness benefit among observed pairs: awareness rose 27.93 percentage points in the assigned arm versus 14.33 in control, an additional 13.59 points (pointwise 95% CI 9.52–17.66; Holm p=1.81e-10).
findings.claim_strength: Supported within the prespecified primary family and observed-pair estimand.
findings.qualification: Assigned/control paired N=960/1016, weighted N=965.21/999.79, ESS=834.41/876.62; eligible N=1400 per arm. Selection into follow-up and item completeness prevents automatic interpretation as a full-cohort or target-population effect.

findings.proposition: Incremental consideration and reported use remain unestablished. Consideration rose 8.356 points assigned versus 8.364 control: contrast −0.008 points (pointwise 95% CI −3.44 to 3.42; Holm p=.996). Usage rose 2.61 versus 3.59 points: contrast −0.98 (−2.70 to 0.74; Holm p=.528).
findings.claim_strength: No statistically supported downstream assignment benefit; absence or equivalence is not established.
findings.qualification: Assigned/control consideration pairs: N=966/1015, weighted N=973.61/1000.17, ESS=839.32/877.62; usage pairs: N=969/1007, weighted N=973.30/993.81, ESS=842.04/868.83. Eligible N=1400 per arm. Intervals describe observed-pair uncertainty, excluding uncertainty from missing-outcome selection. Control growth cannot be attributed to one particular mechanism.

findings.proposition: Selective follow-up materially limits generalisation: 1019 assigned and 1070 control households returned, with weighted return rates of 72.38% and 75.98%. Returners had higher baseline consideration (30.13% versus 21.99%) and digital confidence (46.34% versus 36.56%), lower high budget pressure (33.68% versus 49.20%), and fewer households with children (32.43% versus 42.31%).
findings.claim_strength: Descriptive evidence of selective follow-up; the direction and size of resulting outcome bias remain unknown.
findings.qualification: Return rates use all 1400 households per arm. Profile eligible N=2089 returners and 711 nonreturners; exact valid N, weighted N, ESS and missing counts are in attrition_audit. Baseline consideration was 29.79% control versus 26.31% assigned before attrition, and 31.48% versus 28.76% among returners. These differences neither invalidate randomisation nor establish ignorable missingness.

findings.proposition: Large recipient and recaller consideration gaps are not campaign lift. Logged recipients led nonrecipients by 19.12 points at follow-up but already led by 19.15 at baseline. Recallers led by 37.24 points at follow-up and 32.35 at baseline.
findings.claim_strength: Descriptive associations with substantial pre-existing differences, not causal receipt or recall effects.
findings.qualification: Receipt/no-receipt pair bases: N=1037/944, weighted N=970.04/1003.75, ESS=903.73/820.43. Recall/no-recall bases: N=844/1040, weighted N=760.65/1107.13, ESS=741.87/906.03; 97 consideration pairs lack valid recall. Each comparison uses the same people at both waves. Recall was asked after outcomes; the widening recall gap also cannot establish causation.

findings.proposition: The arms differed in delivery and recall, but neither formed a clean exposed/unexposed group: logged receipt was 70.16% assigned versus 24.54% control; recall was 48.61% versus 32.97%. Among returned valid-recall respondents, 65.82% of logged recipients recalled the campaign, as did 15.73% without logged receipt.
findings.qualification: Receipt uses all enrolled households. Recall valid N=973 assigned and 1014 control, excluding 46/56 numeric-missing answers and 381/330 nonreturners. Concordance bases are 1048 logged recipients and 939 nonrecipients. Exact eligible/valid weighted N and ESS are in receipt_recall_and_selection. Receipt is not proven attention; recall is not verified exposure.

findings.proposition: Households with children report greater meal-planning stress, but superior campaign responsiveness is unestablished. Very/extremely stressful responses were 56.48% with children versus 36.56% without. Children-household assignment contrasts were +10.15 points awareness (pointwise 95% CI 3.52–16.79), +2.95 consideration (−2.90 to 8.80), and +0.91 usage (−2.30 to 4.12). No children-versus-no-children interaction was supported.
findings.claim_strength: Descriptive audience need; no supported differential response in the prespecified interaction family.
findings.qualification: Stress valid N=1060 with children and 1686 without; weighted N=950.38/1791.67, ESS=958.69/1451.12. Children assigned/control pairs are 369/350 awareness, 368/352 consideration and 369/345 usage; all four-cell bases are in children_need_and_heterogeneity. Interaction estimates are −5.07, +4.27 and +2.81 points, with pointwise 95% CIs [−13.46,3.32], [−2.95,11.48] and [−0.98,6.59], and Holm p=.472/.472/.438. Subgroup pointwise intervals do not establish targeting superiority.

findings.proposition: Selected recallers generally rated the message positively: agreement was 76.74% for clarity, 75.90% for believability and 70.52% for relevance. Relevance is a possible creative-test hypothesis; its numerical ranking does not establish a weakness or show that improving it would increase usage.
findings.claim_strength: Descriptive diagnostic evidence supporting a test hypothesis only.
findings.qualification: Eligible recallers N=891, weighted N=800.64, ESS=781.76. Clarity/believability/relevance valid N=862/852/854, weighted N=773.02/765.17/770.28, ESS=755.96/749.26/747.66. Full distributions and missingness are in selected_recaller_diagnostics. Pairwise correlations of .504–.544 describe shared ratings, not causal drivers; nonrecallers were not asked.

findings.proposition: Recorded current users reported favourable experience: 87.74% were satisfied, and mean use was 3.49 days in the previous week. This describes selected users and does not explain or overturn the unestablished incremental usage result.
findings.claim_strength: Descriptive evidence confined to the recorded-user route.
findings.qualification: Eligible users N=208, weighted N=178.30, ESS=184.55. Satisfaction valid N=202, weighted N=172.14, ESS=180.04; usage-days valid N=201, weighted N=172.69, ESS=178.04. Numeric missing N=6/7 respectively; 2592 respondents were structurally outside the route. No assignment comparison or evidence about nonusers is provided.

findings.proposition: A further controlled test is supported as a learning decision: specify an awareness objective, power the downstream question against a prespecified meaningful consideration/use threshold, and improve follow-up retention. Retain households with children as the planned priority audience without declaring them campaign winners. Sales, ROI and superior targeting remain unestablished.
findings.claim_strength: Research recommendation inferred from supported awareness change, downstream uncertainty and selective follow-up.
findings.qualification: This recommends further learning, not a proven commercial rollout. Consideration is not purchasing; reported usage is not verified activity or sales; costs and revenue are absent. The exploratory older, digitally confident online-grocery subgroup has only 22 control and 21 assigned awareness pairs: insufficient base. No effectiveness conclusion is available for that cut.

beats.headline_intent: Awareness increased beyond control; incremental consideration and use remain unestablished.
beats.analytical_relationship: Compare assigned and control changes separately for each endpoint, using paired bases, pointwise intervals and primary-family Holm adjustment.

beats.headline_intent: Limit the conclusion to observed pairs and recognise selective follow-up.
beats.analytical_relationship: Qualify outcome interpretation through arm return rates, item completeness and baseline differences between returners and nonreturners.

beats.headline_intent: Separate delivery and recall from evidence of effectiveness.
beats.analytical_relationship: Show crossover and measurement disagreement, then compare observational consideration gaps with the gaps already present at baseline.

beats.headline_intent: Use audience need and selected respondent feedback to inform hypotheses.
beats.analytical_relationship: Distinguish descriptive stress, message ratings and user experience from differential campaign effectiveness or causal explanations.

beats.headline_intent: Proceed through a focused follow-up experiment with better outcome recovery.
beats.analytical_relationship: Translate supported awareness evidence and unresolved downstream and selection questions into a bounded research recommendation.

method_notes: Review used only the four study texts supplied in the prompt. No tools, external sources, file discovery, raw respondent data or delegated agents were used. Analysis claims summarise approved tables; they are not independently recomputed respondent-level estimates.

Change log: retained the draft's supported primary results, exposure-selection argument and cautious recommendation. Added explicit priority-audience intervals, the children imbalance in follow-up, and the omitted recorded-user experience distributions with a context-only finding. Clarified that the suppressed exploratory table concerns awareness, not evidence for every outcome. Added returned-but-unpaired counts to separate item completeness from nonreturn.
All participants, the service and target profile are fictional. The eligible online-recontact frame is not a national probability sample; these estimates do not describe real UK prevalence.

Primary estimates preserve original assignment among each endpoint's own valid observed pairs. Both wave levels and change use those same pairs. No joint-completeness requirement or conditioning on receipt, recall, satisfaction or contact attempts is imposed. Consideration was asked of everyone after the same neutral description at each wave; outcomes preceded recall.

weight_base is a fixed baseline age-by-online-grocery profile weight, normalised once across enrolment. Weighted N is a sample weight total, not a population count. Kish ESS describes weight concentration and is not outcome precision or an adjustment for attrition.

Inference follows the supplied independent-household fixed-weight paired-change variance: within-arm V=[n/(n−1)]×sum(w²(D−mu)²)/(sum(w))²; contrast SE is 100×sqrt(V_assigned+V_control). Intervals are pointwise 95% normal intervals and p-values are two-sided normal tests. Reported primary and interaction variances are nondegenerate.

Holm adjustment controls each declared three-test family separately at .05: PRIMARY_ASSIGNMENT and SECONDARY_CHILDREN_HETEROGENEITY. It does not provide joint error control over both families or exploratory comparisons. Subgroup pointwise intervals are not multiplicity-adjusted evidence of targeting superiority.

Binary validity is 0/1. Consideration top-two-box is valid 4/5, with valid 1/2/3 coded zero. Codes 97/98/99 and structural blanks are excluded, never imputed as No or zero. Numeric missingness and structural exclusions are separate; baseline and follow-up missing counts can overlap and must not be summed to derive pair exclusions.

Wave-valid and paired distributions remain separate. Full five-category primary consideration and message distributions are retained. Binary No percentages are complements of Yes. Display rounding can prevent categories summing to 100 or rounded levels reproducing rounded changes exactly.

Every reported quantitative comparison meets the constituent-cell N>=40 rule; none requires the N<75 or ESS<50 warning. The exploratory older digital online-grocery awareness comparison is suppressed because its arm pair counts are 22 and 21. Other outcomes for this cut are not supplied and are not assumed absent or zero.

Remaining limits: table-level review cannot verify respondent-level computation. Approximate inference excludes target-profile uncertainty and nonresponse-selection uncertainty. No full-cohort effect, causal receipt effect, IV/CACE estimate, mediation, equivalence, actual-sales effect or ROI is established. Selected-recaller and selected-user diagnostics cannot establish effectiveness or represent people outside their routes; recommendations remain research judgments.
